Restaurant revenue.heading: Cost of Restaurant Revenue
Restaurant revenue.text: Cost of restaurant revenue decreased $13.2 million, or 3.6%, in the year ended December 31, 2025 from 2024. Cost of restaurant revenue decreased $103.7 million, or 21.8%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 from 2023. Cost of restaurant revenue as a percentage of restaurant revenue was approximately 91.7%, 88.5%, and 88.6% in the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. The increase in cost of restaurant revenue as a percentage of restaurant revenue in 2025 compared to 2024 was primarily attributable to an increase in the cost of meats and poultry at 99 Restaurants of 0.7 percentage points and 0.7 percentage points , respectively, and an increase in the cost of labor and meats at O'Charley's of 2.6 percentage points and 0.8 percentage points, respectively. The decrease in cost of restaurant revenue in 2024 compared to 2023 is primarily attributable to the closure of 77 O'Charley's stores during the year ended December 31, 2023.

intro.text: The following describes the business of Cannae Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries. Except where otherwise noted, all references to "we," "us," "our," "Cannae," "Cannae Holdings" or the "Company," are to Cannae Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries, taken together. We primarily acquire interests in operating companies and are engaged in actively managing and operating a core group of those companies, which we are committed to supporting for the long term. From time to time, we also seek to take meaningful equity ownership stakes where we have the ability to control or significantly influence quality companies, and we bring the strength of our operational expertise to each of our subsidiaries.

opex.heading: Other Operating Expenses
opex.text: Other operating expenses increased by $7.6 million, or 28.7%, in the year ended December 31, 2025 from 2024. Other operating expenses decreased by $49.4 million, or 65.1%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 from 2023. The increase in the year ended December 31, 2025 from 2024 is primarily attributable to a $12.2 million increase in non-cash impairments to property, plant and equipment and lease assets primarily associated with O'Charley's, partially offset by a reduction in back office costs at the Restaurant Group's headquarters. tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income tax expense (benefit) was $13.0 million, $3.3 million, and $(71.5) million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. The effective tax rate for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 was (6.8)%, (1.3)%, and 35.7%, respectively. The fluctuation in income tax benefit as a percentage of loss before income taxes is attributable to our estimate of ultimate income tax liability or benefit and changes in the characteristics of net earnings or loss year to year, such as the weighting of operating income versus investment income and the varying impact of equity in earnings or loss of unconsolidated affiliates on pre-tax income or loss. The change in our effective tax rate in the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to 2024 is primarily attributable to the recognition of tax losses of $281.1 million that will be carried back to 2022 to refund excess capital gains, offset by the recording of additional valuation allowance in the amount of $108.8 million on the deferred tax assets related to our investments and our federal net operating losses.

Restaurant revenue.heading: Cost of Restaurant Revenue
Restaurant revenue.text: Cost of restaurant revenue decreased $13.2 million, or 3.6%, in the year ended December 31, 2025 from 2024. Cost of restaurant revenue decreased $103.7 million, or 21.8%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 from 2023. Cost of restaurant revenue as a percentage of restaurant revenue was approximately 91.7%, 88.5%, and 88.6% in the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. The increase in cost of restaurant revenue as a percentage of restaurant revenue in 2025 compared to 2024 was primarily attributable to an increase in the cost of meats and poultry at 99 Restaurants of 0.7 percentage points and 0.7 percentage points , respectively, and an increase in the cost of labor and meats at O'Charley's of 2.6 percentage points and 0.8 percentage points, respectively. The decrease in cost of restaurant revenue in 2024 compared to 2023 is primarily attributable to the closure of 77 O'Charley's stores during the year ended December 31, 2023.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
